name: Aluminum sheet
blurb: Light metal from the shed. It holds a vacuum, and it melts far below Venus.
sourceNote: Density is the usual 2700 kg/m³ for aluminum. Yield, conductivity, and melting point are typical 6061 handbook values, not NASA planet data.

name: Steel scrap
blurb: Heavy and strong. It conducts heat so well that a bare steel shell cooks or freezes you.
sourceNote: Mild-steel handbook values: about 7850 kg/m³, yield near 250 MPa, conductivity near 50 W/m·K.

name: Aerogel blanket
blurb: Almost no heat gets through. Too weak to hold pressure by itself.
sourceNote: Silica aerogel blanket: low density and conductivity around 0.015 W/m·K. It is insulation, not a pressure shell.

name: Wool batting
blurb: Enough for a short cold stay. It chars long before Venus.
sourceNote: Wool batting is a poor structural material. Conductivity is about 0.04 W/m·K, and it scorches well below 200 °C.

name: Oxygen cylinders
blurb: Earth air does not come with you. This is the oxygen you can bottle and carry.
sourceNote: The gas is oxygen. A full cylinder in this yard holds 2 kg, about two days of one person's breathing at the NASA life-support planning rate.
